capability_summary: Designs a promotional offer or campaign for a telecoms/connectivity provider and verifies it against the provider's own commercial rules — margin floors, discount-approval thresholds, contract and regulatory constraints — before it is cleared for market.
user_goal: Get a promotional offer that is attractive enough to sell but provably compliant with the business's margin floor and commercial rules, with the arithmetic shown so a reviewer can confirm the verdict rather than trust it.
success_looks_like: Every promotional price is traced to an explicit cost basis and an explicit margin calculation a reviewer can re-add by hand.
The pass/fail margin verdict is computed on the highest-cost defensible reading of the offer, not a favourable one.
Any lower-cost reading appears only as clearly labelled sensitivity analysis that cannot be mistaken for the verdict.
Assumptions about subscriber volume tier, speed-tier pairing, tax basis and which per-service charges apply are stated before the figures that depend on them.
Arithmetic is internally consistent with every stated assumption, with no figure carried over from a different assumption set.
Offers that breach the margin floor are reported as failing with the shortfall quantified, not silently repriced or reframed.
Rules that cannot be satisfied simultaneously are surfaced as a conflict requiring a business decision, not resolved by quietly dropping one.
Discounts above the approval threshold are flagged with the approving authority named, not applied unilaterally.
Promotional duration, eligibility, contract term and reversion price are specified so the offer can be operationalised without further guessing.
A reviewer can locate, in one pass, the cost line, the price line, the margin line and the floor being tested.

priority_qualities.quality: Verdict computed on the highest-cost defensible basis
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: A pass obtained by choosing the cheapest reading is the single failure mode that puts loss-making offers into market.

priority_qualities.quality: Arithmetic that reconciles line by line
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: An unverifiable margin number is indistinguishable from a wrong one and cannot clear a commercial gate.

priority_qualities.quality: Assumptions stated before, and consistent with, the figures they drive
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: Disclosure is only a guard if the numbers actually follow the assumption declared.

priority_qualities.quality: Complete inclusion of every mandatory cost component
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: Omitting a recurring per-service or per-subscriber charge inflates margin and is the most common silent error.

priority_qualities.quality: Explicit handling of rule conflicts and threshold breaches
priority_qualities.why_it_matters: A conflict resolved silently transfers a commercial decision from the business to the tool.
Duration, eligibility and reversion terms determine whether the modelled margin survives contact with billing.
A compliant offer nobody buys wastes the promotional window.
Verification speed determines whether the check actually happens before launch.

constraints: State the cost basis and every included component before quoting any margin figure.
Compute the margin verdict on the highest-cost defensible reading available from the inputs and rules.
Label any lower-cost reading explicitly as sensitivity analysis and keep it visually and structurally separate from the verdict.
Name each assumption (volume tier, speed-tier pairing, tax basis, applicable per-service charges) at the point it first affects a number.
Reject any assumption that contradicts the governing commercial rules rather than disclosing it and proceeding.
Show the subtraction or division that produces each margin percentage or amount.
Test the resulting margin against the stated floor and report pass or fail in words, not by implication.
Quantify the shortfall in currency and percentage points whenever the floor is missed.
Identify the approving authority whenever a discount exceeds the delegated threshold.
Report mutually unsatisfiable rules as an unresolved conflict with the specific rules named.
Express monetary figures in the provider's currency and stated tax basis consistently throughout.
State promotional duration, eligible base, contract term and post-promotion reversion price for every offer.
never_do: Never publish a margin verdict derived from a lower-cost reading when a higher-cost defensible reading exists.
Never treat declaring an assumption as licence for arithmetic that is wrong under that assumption.
Never adopt an assumption that conflicts with the governing commercial rules.
Never omit a mandatory cost component from the verdict basis, including recurring per-service and per-subscriber charges.
Never mix figures computed under different assumption sets within one calculation.
Never present sensitivity analysis in a position or format where it could be read as the verdict.
Never reframe a floor breach as acceptable without naming it as a breach first.
Never apply a discount above the approval threshold without flagging the required approval.
Never silently drop one of two conflicting rules to manufacture a satisfiable offer.
Never switch tax basis mid-calculation or leave the basis unstated.
Never assert a figure as verified without showing the operation that produces it.
Never present an untested or unverifiable offer as cleared for market.
objective_invariants: A named cost basis with an itemised component list appears before the first margin figure.
Every mandatory cost component listed in the cost-basis formula is present in the verdict calculation or explicitly justified as inapplicable.
The verdict calculation uses the highest-cost reading; each alternative reading is labelled as sensitivity analysis.
Each stated assumption is followed by figures that arithmetically follow from it.
Each margin figure is accompanied by the arithmetic that produces it, reproducible by hand.
A pass/fail statement against the margin floor appears in words for every offer.
Any floor breach is accompanied by a shortfall quantified in both currency and percentage points.
Any discount above the approval threshold is accompanied by the named approving authority.
Any pair of rules that cannot both be satisfied is named as a conflict, with both rules identified.
Currency and tax basis are stated once and used identically in every subsequent figure.
Promotional duration, eligibility, contract term and reversion price are each stated for every offer.
No figure appears without either a source input, a stated assumption, or a shown derivation.

cost_basis_formula.formula: Total promotional cost = wholesale/access cost for the paired speed tier at the applicable subscriber-volume tier + all recurring per-service charges that apply to that service + all per-subscriber charges over the promotional term, expressed on a single consistent tax basis; promotional margin = (promotional revenue over the term - total promotional cost over the term) / promotional revenue over the term.
mandatory_components: Wholesale or network access cost for the specific speed tier being promoted
Subscriber-volume tier applied to that access cost, with the tier stated
Every recurring per-service charge applicable to the service being promoted
Every per-subscriber charge applicable over the promotional term
Any one-off acquisition, installation or hardware cost amortised across the stated term
The promotional term length used to annualise or total both cost and revenue
A single declared tax basis applied identically to cost and revenue
Post-promotion reversion price where it affects the term being evaluated
cost_basis_formula.verdict_basis_rule: The pass/fail verdict against the margin floor must be computed on the highest-cost defensible reading permitted by the inputs and the governing commercial rules - the least favourable applicable volume tier, the least favourable defensible speed-tier pairing, and the inclusion of every per-service and per-subscriber charge whose applicability is not positively excluded; lower-cost readings may be shown only as separately labelled sensitivity analysis and may never determine the verdict.
cost_basis_formula.assumption_disclosure_rule: An assumption must be stated at the point it first affects a figure, must not contradict the governing commercial rules, and must be followed by arithmetic that is internally consistent with it; disclosure never excuses a calculation that is wrong under the assumption disclosed, never substitutes for choosing the highest-cost defensible basis for the verdict, and an assumption that conflicts with a governing rule must be rejected rather than declared.

scope_in: Designing promotional offers, bundles, discounts and campaign mechanics for connectivity and telecoms services
Deriving the cost basis for a promoted service from wholesale, per-service and per-subscriber inputs
Testing a proposed promotional price against the margin floor and reporting the verdict
Identifying discount-approval thresholds and the authority required to clear them
Surfacing conflicts between commercial, contractual and regulatory rules that constrain an offer
Specifying promotional duration, eligibility, contract term and reversion mechanics
Producing sensitivity analysis across volume tiers, speed-tier pairings and tax bases
Recommending offer adjustments that bring a failing offer above the floor
scope_out: Executing, scheduling or publishing the campaign to any channel
Producing final customer-facing creative, artwork or ad copy as the primary deliverable
Approving a discount that exceeds the delegated threshold
Negotiating or amending wholesale supplier rates
Legal or regulatory sign-off on promotional terms
Forecasting demand uplift or campaign response rates as authoritative figures
Setting or revising the margin floor itself
activation_expectations: Triggers on requests to design, price, discount or evaluate a promotional offer or campaign for connectivity services.
Triggers when asked whether a proposed promotional price clears the margin floor.
Triggers on requests to check an existing offer against commercial rules before launch.
Triggers when a bundle, free-months, waived-installation or reduced-rate mechanic is proposed.
Requests the margin floor, wholesale inputs and applicable charges when they are not supplied rather than inventing them.
States explicitly when an input is missing and what the verdict depends on.
Does not trigger for pure creative or copywriting requests with no pricing component.
Does not trigger for post-launch campaign performance reporting.
non_qualities: Length or verbosity - a short verified offer beats a long one.
Confident tone - assertion is not verification and does not raise a figure's credibility.
Number of sections or headings produced.
Completeness of a document template, where filled sections carry no verified arithmetic.
Sophistication of marketing language or campaign naming.
Visual formatting, tables or styling beyond what aids reviewer verification.
